senses.gloss: a general permission given in advance
gloss_distractors: a detailed review by outside auditors
senses.definition: Permission given once in advance to cover a whole class of decisions.
senses.caution: Claim it only if you are sure, because people will check and there are usually conditions.
senses.example: We do not have blanket approval for production data, it is per use case, and the last one took three weeks.

cues.text: A team believes one sign-off last quarter covers every future use of customer data, and you need the phrase for what they think they have.
You are drafting a governance note and need the phrase for a single sign-off that covers a whole class of decisions, so none of them needs a case-by-case review.
Legal says any vendor under a set spend can be onboarded without a fresh review each time, and you want the phrase for that.

distractors: Approval that expires if it is not used within a set period.
A decision taken by one person and announced without discussion.
A rule that applies to everyone except those who ask to be excused.
A requirement that every single case be reviewed on its own before it can proceed.
A standing instruction to stop work the moment a particular threshold is crossed.

senses.definition: Full freedom to act as you judge best, usually approval given in advance for everything.
senses.caution: Said about yourself it sounds boastful, and about others it suggests nobody is checking their work. Use it when the freedom really is complete.
senses.example: The new CTO gave the platform team carte blanche on tooling for the first year.

cues.text: A sponsor offers to let you make all the tooling decisions for the year without coming back to him each time.
A friend's parents have told her to plan the anniversary party however she likes, with no limit on the budget.
A neighbour is letting the builder choose every fitting in the new kitchen, with no say in it at all.

distractors: A written warning given before any formal action is taken.
Permission for one specific case, which has to be asked for again next time.
A rule that every decision above a set amount goes to a committee first.
A budget that has been frozen until the next planning round, with no exceptions made for anyone.
A requirement that each change be reviewed by two people before it goes live, however small it is.
